name: CSW Title
epitaph: CSW's own top belt, contested from January 1996 as the "CSW World Title" and renamed the plain "CSW Title" that August. Tank won it first, eliminating Mercury in a battle royal, and said so himself afterwards — "Tank was a rookie when he came too the csw and became the 1st world champion." Nine independent-era reigns survive on the fed's own numbered ledger, all recorded here; six men held it, Mr. Ravishing twice. The Heartbreaker's own bio insists he was the second of them and Tank the man he beat, where the ledger puts Ace Stevens between the two — a disagreement kept rather than settled. Shane Curton was defending it in February 2004 when Pres Burns, having acquired the CSW Efed outright, stripped it from him and folded the lineage into his own CWF-Pro hierarchy; the belt's later CWF-Pro-branded life is recorded on CWF-Pro's own title row.

name: CSW National Title
epitaph: CSW's own second-tier singles belt, contested from January 1996, and the deepest of its four lineages at fourteen independent-era reigns — all recorded here. Mercury won it first, eliminating a young Miguel Sanchez in a battle royal, and the feud that opened it ran on: "It was always Sanchez vs Mercury," his own bio says, "They have been in a feud for over 2 years." Sanchez took it twice, and was named the Icon on the second. Bermuda Billy Page's own bio independently confirms the ledger down to the ordinal — "Billy became the 2nd man to win the CSW National title." Tom Cage was on his second reign when the acquisition stripped him of it in February 2004, still trying to get the CSW's own office to sign him a champion-versus-champion match against the TPW. Four further wrestlers — Charlie, Jack Kelly, Prowler and Reefer King — claim this championship on their own bio cards and appear nowhere in its fourteen reigns; those claims are recorded on their own tenures, not here.

name: CSW Royal Title
epitaph: CSW's own third singles belt, contested from March 1996 — the only one of the four whose header does not start with the promotion. Kevin McFly won it first, eliminating Miguel Sanchez in a battle royal ("He did become the 1st Royal champion," his own bio agrees, in a career he says he otherwise made no name in). Eight independent-era reigns survive on the fed's own numbered ledger, all recorded here, eight different men — the only CSW belt no one ever won twice. Facing Death's own bio credits the stable rather than the man for his: "The UBH did help him win the CSW Royal title. His only title he ever won." Mike Hart was defending it in February 2004 when the acquisition stripped him of it, though the prose on his own page names a different belt than his own card does.

name: CSW World Tag Team Title
epitaph: CSW's own tag belt, contested from January 1996 as the "CSW Tag Team Title" and renamed "CSW World Tag Team Title" that August. The Raxton Brothers won it first, throwing the Pretty Boys out of a battle royal, and dominated its whole independent-era run — three of nine recorded reigns by the ledger's own count, plus a fourth spell the ledger pointedly does NOT number, restored to them after the CSW itself stripped UBH's disputed house-show win and handed the belts back. (Zamza, one half of that UBH team, tells it differently on his own page: the match never happened, and the promotion closed before the pay-per-view could.) This ledger keeps more of the promotion's texture than any of the other three: the only reign length CSW's entire record preserves — the Kennel Killers' 22 days, its longest, by a team whose members are named nowhere at all — and the note that Crippler, one half of "Rico Suave & Crippler," was the belt's own first Black champion. The Raxton Brothers were still champions in February 2004 when the acquisition stripped the lineage and folded it into CWF-Pro's own tag belt.
